answer: A trellis gives a vine its shape the way a mutual-insurance syndicate gives an agent identity its shape: to join, an agent stakes funds into a small shared pool with strangers, and fraud by any member slashes the whole pool. Members therefore vet newcomers ruthlessly and keep groups tiny, because each new face risks everyone's money. A lone operator trying to run a meadow of fake identities must fund a separate pool for every clone and find honest members willing to share risk with them. Honest agents gain cheap standing from the crystal-clear record of a syndicate that has never paid a claim.
